# Helpdesk One: final project report

Prepared for Sofia Marin, project sponsor, from the project folder. Where documents conflict, plan v2 FINAL (10 March 2026), change request CR-03, budget-final.csv, the final vendor invoice and the handover checklist of 5 August 2026 are treated as current.

## Executive summary

Helpdesk One replaced the two regional helpdesks (North and South) and their two ticket systems with one desk on one platform, Deskwise. It went live on 22 June 2026, three weeks later than the first target of 1 June, and closed hypercare on 17 July. The final approved budget is $92,000 and the actual spend is $82,800, which leaves $9,200 unspent. All five tracked service measures improved between January to March 2026 and July 2026.

Two handover items are still open and have no owner: the decommissioning of the legacy North and South ticket systems (no date set) and the weekly KPI report to operations.

*Figure 1 (in out/report.html): service measures before and after the move.*

## Budget outcome

The kickoff budget was $85,000 (plan v1). Change request CR-03, raised by Pavel Novak on 3 March and approved by Sofia Marin on 5 March 2026, added a phone integration for $7,000 and raised the approved budget to $92,000. The South desk takes about a third of its contacts by phone, so without the integration agents would have had to log those calls by hand.

| Line | Approved (USD) | Actual (USD) | Difference (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Platform licences | 36,000 | 36,000 | 0 |
| Migration vendor | 22,000 | 18,400 | 3,600 under |
| Phone integration | 7,000 | 7,900 | 900 over |
| Training | 9,000 | 7,400 | 1,600 under |
| Internal backfill | 14,000 | 13,100 | 900 under |
| Contingency | 4,000 | 0 | 4,000 unspent |
| Total | 92,000 | 82,800 | 9,200 under |

The project spent 90% of the approved budget. The migration vendor's fixed price of $18,400 matches the final invoice, which Karl Osei approved on 31 July 2026, with no change orders. The phone integration is the only line that overran, by $900.

*Figure 2 (in out/report.html): approved and actual spend by line.*

## Schedule

Plan v2 FINAL supersedes plan v1 of 2 February 2026. The move from 1 June to 22 June, a slip of 21 days, came from CR-03.

| Task | Start | End | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| Requirements | 19 January | 27 February | Karl Osei |
| Data migration | 2 March | 22 May | Datamove Ltd |
| Phone integration | 6 April | 5 June | Pavel Novak |
| Training | 1 June | 19 June | Nadia Haddad |
| Go-live | 22 June | 22 June | Karl Osei |
| Hypercare | 22 June | 17 July | Karl Osei |
| Closure | 31 July | 31 July | Sofia Marin |

*Figure 3 (in out/report.html): plan v2 FINAL timeline with the 1 June target marked.*

## Scope and delivery

- The migration covered tickets from the last 24 months, 38,500 tickets in total. Older tickets stay in the legacy archives. This was decided at the 17 February meeting and confirmed on 3 March.
- Datamove removed 2,300 duplicate tickets from the South export, which took longer than expected.
- 14 agents moved to the new desk. The field-service queue was out of scope.
- Two extra training sessions for the South desk, agreed on 19 May, addressed agents who preferred the old tool.
- Hypercare ran from 22 June to 17 July. 126 migration-related issues were logged and all but 2 were closed.

## Service results

| Measure | Before (January to March 2026) | After (July 2026) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Average first response time | 9.5 hours | 2.8 hours | 6.7 hours faster (71%) |
| Open backlog | 410 tickets | 65 tickets | 345 fewer (84%) |
| Customer satisfaction | 71% | 88% | 17 pp higher |
| Cost per ticket | $14.20 | $9.80 | $4.40 lower (31%) |
| Tickets handled per agent per day | 17 | 26 | 53% more |

## Lessons learned

What worked:

- Migrating only the last 24 months kept the data work to 38,500 tickets.
- Extra training sessions for the South desk removed most resistance before go-live.
- Hypercare caught the migration-related issues quickly.

What did not work:

- The phone integration was added late through CR-03. It cost $7,000 plus a three-week delay and overran by $900. Ask about phone and chat channels when gathering requirements.
- The South export was full of duplicates. Check data quality before the migration window is fixed.

Do next time: freeze scope before the plan is baselined, and sample each source system before agreeing a migration date.

| Item | Owner | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Runbook handed to the operations team | Nadia Haddad | done |
| Agent accounts and permissions audited | Karl Osei | done |
| Final vendor invoice approved | Karl Osei | done, 31 July |
| Hypercare closed | Karl Osei | done, 17 July |
| Decommission the legacy North and South ticket systems | no owner assigned | open, date not set |
| Weekly KPI report to operations | no owner assigned | open, format agreed |

[ASK AUTHOR: who owns the decommissioning of the legacy ticket systems, and by what date? Who owns the weekly KPI report?]

## Note on the source documents

The folder held two copies of plan v1, two identical KPI files, a May newsletter that still gave 1 June as the go-live date and a brief for an unrelated project. The superseded plan and the newsletter were not used for current dates or figures, and the unrelated brief was left out.
